history.period: Older monastery pre-existed; present monastery completed 1740; rebuilt 1977
history.summary: THIS IS A BUDDHIST MONASTERY (KARMA KAGYU), NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. Phodong Monastery at Phodong, Mangan district, North Sikkim (~28-39 km from Gangtok at ~4,500 ft; CSV town 'Mangan' acceptable), is a Kagyupa (Karma Kagyu) monastery. An older monastery pre-existed on the site; the present one was begun by Chogyal Gyurmed Namgyal (4th king) and completed in 1740, and 9th Karmapa tradition claims the founding of Rumtek, Phodong and Ralang. The earthquake-damaged old structure was dismantled and rebuilt bigger in 1977 with state aid; experts from the Delhi National Museum rescued the old frescoes, and it was reconstructed again under Sidkeong Tulku Namgyal. It is famous for its ancient murals and frescoes - the Sikkim ecclesiastical department notes Alexandra David-Neel studied here in 1912. About 260 monks reside here.

name: Phodong Monastery
town_description: Phodong, about 28-39 km from Gangtok in Mangan district, is one of North Sikkim's principal monastic villages. The monastery stands at ~4,500 ft with views over the North Sikkim hills. Nearby: Labrang Monastery (2 km) and Kabi Lungchok, the historic site of the 13th-century Lepcha-Bhutia blood-brotherhood treaty.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan, Karma Kagyu) - NOT a Hindu temple
